text: A workstation on Castellan Retail's Workstations VLAN has been quietly sending small amounts of data to an external IP address every 25 to 30 minutes for nine days. No single transfer is larger than three megabytes, well under any volume-based threshold the SOC has configured, which is exactly why it's still running undetected by anything that only watches size.

Lesson 11's baselining work catches this first. The workstation normally sends under five megabytes a day, almost entirely to known corporate SaaS destinations. The flow platform doesn't flag any single transfer, it flags the pattern: a brand-new destination this host has never talked to before, contacted on a suspiciously regular interval, over and over.

The analyst checks the destination IP against Castellan's threat intelligence feed from Lesson 18. It's a listed indicator of compromise, attributed to infrastructure associated with a known data-theft toolkit. On its own a flagged IP is a lead, not proof, but combined with the flow deviation it moves this from odd traffic to investigate now.

EDR telemetry shows the connections aren't coming from a browser at all. They're coming from an executable in a user-writable temp folder, named to look like a normal Windows process. The process tree shows a Word document opened nine days ago spawning a command shell, which launched the disguised process running from the wrong location entirely.

None of the three signals alone was conclusive: the flow deviation could have been a new SaaS tool, the flagged IP could have been stale, and the disguised process might have sat in a queue of lower-priority alerts without the matching outbound pattern. Together they confirm a disguised process is exfiltrating data on a schedule to known-bad infrastructure.

The response follows Lesson 16's containment playbook: isolate the host via EDR without disturbing evidence, block the destination IP at the perimeter NGFW, preserve the binary and the original document, and sweep that IOC against every other host's flow and EDR history. Next up, a full capstone review tying all seven chapters together.
